items.heading: The Rights of Persons
items.text: The Rights of Persons The Rights of Persons The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (the RPwD Act) is the main law. It replaced the 1995 Act, was notified in December 2016 and recognises 21 specified disabilities. The table shows the sections that matter most for study and work.

items.heading: Exam Help Is the Part
items.text: Exam help is the part students most often learn about too late. The two rule sets below are the ones most families meet. Always read the bulletin of the exact exam.

visuals.heading: What the Law Gives You, and What

rows: The Act lists 21 specified disabilities. A benchmark disability means not less than 40 percent of a specified disability, certified by a certifying authority (Section 2(r)).
Reservations and most scholarships start at 40 percent. Below 40 percent you can still get exam help if writing is hard (see the exam section).
Section 31: every child with a benchmark disability aged six to eighteen has the right to free education in a neighbourhood school or a special school of choice.
Ask the school for admission and support in writing, and keep a copy.

Section 32: government institutions of higher education, and other institutions that receive government aid, must reserve not less than five percent of seats for persons with benchmark disabilities. Admission also carries an upper age relaxation of five years.
The section names government and aided institutions. For a private unaided college, read its own prospectus; do not assume the 5 percent applies.

Section 34: every government establishment must fill not less than four percent of vacancies with persons with benchmark disabilities, in the posts identified for each disability. One percent each goes to blindness and low vision; deaf and hard of hearing; and locomotor disability (including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy). One percent goes to autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability, mental illness and multiple disabilities together.
The law sets a floor, not a job. Each recruitment notice lists which posts are identified for which disability, and a post can be closed to your category.

figures.label: Growth Rate
figures.source: Two changes matter. On 15 October 2024 the Supreme Court held in Omkar Ramchandra Gond v Union of India that a disability of 40 percent or more does not by itself bar MBBS, and that a board must record whether the disability would actually prevent the course. On 27 July 2026 the NMC issued guidelines that judge functional ability, with an Eligibility Certificate that can say Eligible, Eligible with Reasonable Accommodation, or Ineligible with reasons.
